elements.requirement: The court must make a disqualification order against a person on an application under section 6 if the statutory conditions regarding directorship and unfitness are satisfied.
elements.quote: The court shall make a disqualification order against a person in any case where, on an application under this section

elements.requirement: To satisfy the condition in section 6(1)(a)(i), the court must be satisfied that the person is or has been a director of a company which has at any time become insolvent, whether while that person was a director or subsequently.
elements.quote: the person is or has been a director of a company which has at any time become insolvent (whether while the person was a director or subsequently)

elements.requirement: To satisfy the condition in section 6(1)(a)(ii), the court must be satisfied that the person has been a director of a company which has at any time been dissolved without becoming insolvent, whether while that person was a director or subsequently.
elements.quote: the person has been a director of a company which has at any time been dissolved without becoming insolvent (whether while the person was a director or subsequently)

elements.requirement: To satisfy the condition in section 6(1)(b), the court must be satisfied that the person's conduct as a director of the relevant company—taken either alone or together with that person's conduct as a director of one or more other companies or overseas companies—makes the person unfit to be concerned in the management of a company.
elements.quote: the person’s conduct as a director of that company (either taken alone or taken together with the person’s conduct as a director of one or more other companies or overseas companies) makes the person unfit to be concerned in the management of a company.

elements.requirement: Where a company or overseas company has become insolvent, references to a person's conduct as a director include that person's conduct in relation to any matter connected with or arising out of the insolvency.
elements.quote: references to a person's conduct as a director of any company or overseas company include, where that company or overseas company has become insolvent, references to that person's conduct in relation to any matter connected with or arising out of the insolvency.

elements.requirement: For the purposes of section 6, a company becomes insolvent if it goes into liquidation at a time when its assets are insufficient for the payment of its debts and other liabilities and the expenses of the winding up.
elements.quote: the company goes into liquidation at a time when its assets are insufficient for the payment of its debts and other liabilities and the expenses of the winding up

elements.requirement: For the purposes of section 6, a company becomes insolvent if it enters administration.
elements.quote: the company enters administration

elements.requirement: For the purposes of section 6, a company becomes insolvent if an administrative receiver of the company is appointed.
elements.quote: an administrative receiver of the company is appointed

elements.requirement: For the purposes of section 6, an overseas company becomes insolvent if it enters into insolvency proceedings of any description, including interim proceedings, in any jurisdiction.
elements.quote: an overseas company becomes insolvent if the company enters into insolvency proceedings of any description (including interim proceedings) in any jurisdiction.

elements.requirement: For the purposes of section 6 and section 7(2), where the company in question is being or has been wound up by the court, the court means that court.
elements.quote: where the company in question is being or has been wound up by the court, that court

elements.requirement: For the purposes of section 6 and section 7(2), where the company in question is being or has been wound up voluntarily, the court means any court which has or had jurisdiction to wind it up.
elements.quote: where the company in question is being or has been wound up voluntarily, any court which has or (as the case may be) had jurisdiction to wind it up

elements.requirement: For the purposes of section 6 and section 7(2), where neither court winding up nor voluntary winding up applies but an administrator or administrative receiver has at any time been appointed in respect of the company in question, the court means any court which has jurisdiction to wind it up.
elements.quote: where neither paragraph (a) nor (b) applies but an administrator or administrative receiver has at any time been appointed in respect of the company in question, any court which has jurisdiction to wind it up

elements.requirement: For the purposes of section 6 and section 7(2), where the company in question has been dissolved without becoming insolvent, the court means a court which had jurisdiction to wind it up at the time it was dissolved.
elements.quote: where the company in question has been dissolved without becoming insolvent, a court which at the time it was dissolved had jurisdiction to wind it up.

elements.requirement: Sections 117 and 120 of the Insolvency Act 1986 apply for the purposes of section 6(3) as if references in the definitions of 'registered office' to the presentation of the petition for winding up were references to the passing of the resolution for voluntary winding up (in a case within subsection (3)(b)) or to the appointment of the administrator or administrative receiver (in a case within subsection (3)(c)).
elements.quote: Sections 117 and 120 of the Insolvency Act 1986 (jurisdiction) shall apply for the purposes of subsection (3) as if the references in the definitions of “registered office” to the presentation of the petition for winding up were references— (a) in a case within paragraph (b) of that subsection, to the passing of the resolution for voluntary winding up, (b) in a case within paragraph (c) of that subsection, to the appointment of the administrator or (as the case may be) administrative receiver.

elements.requirement: Proceedings are not invalidated under subsection (3) solely because they are taken in the wrong court.
elements.quote: Nothing in subsection (3) invalidates any proceedings by reason of their being taken in the wrong court

elements.requirement: Proceedings for or in connection with a disqualification order under section 6, or in connection with a disqualification undertaking accepted under section 7, may be retained in the court where they were commenced even if that court was not the court in which they ought to have been commenced.
elements.quote: proceedings— (a) for or in connection with a disqualification order under this section, or (b) in connection with a disqualification undertaking accepted under section 7, may be retained in the court in which the proceedings were commenced, although it may not be the court in which they ought to have been commenced.

elements.requirement: In section 6 and section 7, the term 'director' includes a shadow director.
elements.quote: In this section and section 7, “director” includes a shadow director

elements.requirement: Under section 6, the minimum period of disqualification is 2 years.
elements.quote: Under this section the minimum period of disqualification is 2 years

elements.requirement: Under section 6, the maximum period of disqualification is 15 years.
elements.quote: the maximum period is 15 years.
